subject: Clarify CCPA/CPRA: service-provider scope & onshore fallback for pilot
messages:
From: Andrea Ruiz <andrea.ruiz@healthops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@healthops.com>, Privacy Team <privacy@healthops.com>
Date: Mon, Aug 02, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot docs - role language question

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the draft DPA. Two quick questions from our side before we circulate to legal:

1) For CCPA/CPRA, we need explicit confirmation Redwood will act only as a service provider (limited-use) for the pilot telemetry and not be permitted to "sell" or "monetize" any derived insights. Can you confirm the proposed language covers that?

2) Our security team asked about an onshore fallback for telemetry persistence/processing in case an offshore subprocessor is unavailable due to maintenance or emergency. Do you have an onshore fallback playbook we can reference, or would we need addendum language?

We attached a short redline (HealthOps marked) and the subprocessors list we received during onboarding. Would appreciate a short note we can forward to legal.

Best,
Andrea
Director, Partnerships
HealthOps

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Ruiz <andrea.ruiz@healthops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Aug 02, 2027 at 11:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot docs - role language question

Andrea — thanks for the clear questions and the redline. Short answers up front: yes, and yes (with options). Details below so your legal/security teams have language to work with.

1) Service provider / limited use under CCPA/CPRA
- Redwood will act as a service provider (we don’t act as a controller). We will only process Personal Information on HealthOps' documented instructions for the pilot and related support, and we will not "sell" Personal Information or use it for cross-customer advertising or enrichment.
- Suggested addendum sentence you can paste into your draft: "Vendor is a Service Provider for purposes of the CCPA/CPRA and shall not sell Personal Information, nor use Personal Information for cross-customer advertising or independent monetization, except as set forth in Section X (Aggregated/De-identified Metrics)."

2) Onshore fallback for telemetry processing
- We maintain onshore fallback capacity for critical telemetry and log retention. Options we can include in an addendum:
  * Onshore fallback clause: "In the event an offshore subprocessor is unavailable for >= 24 hours, Vendor will failover telemetry collection and short-term processing to an onshore processor to preserve SLA-bound retention and supportability."
  * Time/bandwidth limits: specify that the fallback is intended for continuity (e.g., up to 72 hours, or for defined incidents), and longer-term needs require written notice.
  * Encryption and key management: onshore fallback environments use the same KMS configurations; we can reference the SOC 2 report for controls.

3) Subprocessors & notice
- We attach our current subprocessors list (PDF). We notify customers per our DPA when adding subprocessors and provide onshore alternatives for customers with strict residency needs.

Next steps I propose:
- Neha can propose concrete redline text (she’s looped) that addresses both the limited-use sentence and a fallback snippet.
- If HealthOps prefers specific SLAs for fallback time-to-failover, we can map that to Dedicated capacity or a contractual add-on.

I’m happy to jump on a 20-min call with your privacy lead if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrea Ruiz <andrea.ruiz@healthops.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Aug 02, 2027 at 13:28 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot docs - role language question

Andrea — draft redline below that you can paste into HealthOps' mark-up. Tried to keep it tight so your lawyers don't need to rework other sections.

Proposed insert (for DPA, new paragraph under "CCPA/CPRA role and restrictions"):
"Vendor is a Service Provider for purposes of the CCPA/CPRA and shall process Personal Information solely on Controller's documented instructions. Vendor shall not sell Personal Information, as defined under applicable state law, and shall not use Personal Information for cross-customer advertising or independent monetization. Vendor may process Aggregated or De-identified Data for product analytics and service improvement, provided such data cannot reasonably be re-identified.

Onshore fallback: In the event a designated subprocessor located outside the United States becomes unavailable for operational reasons, Vendor shall failover telemetry collection and short-term processing to onshore infrastructure for the sole purpose of continuity and compliance with Controller's retention obligations. Failover shall be limited to 72 hours unless Controller requests an extension in writing. Vendor will notify Controller within four (4) hours of failover initiation and provide a post-incident summary."

If HealthOps wants a shorter 24-hour failover SLA, we can accommodate that on Dedicated or as a Service Level Addendum.

Grace — FYI, if HealthOps is okay with the 72-hour default we don't need an expanded commercial term here.

—Neha

Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

- Confirming the SOC 2 report and subprocessors list are current (we received the PDF attached earlier).
- We’ll accept the 72-hour default for continuity, with an option to request a 24-hour SLA on Dedicated.

I’m going to send this to our legal and procurement teams; procurement will follow up with a DocuSign request if everything looks good. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Andrea
